recap:
Brighton edges out Manchester United with 2-1.

Brighton dominated the ball, holding 49.1% possession against Manchester United’s 50.9%. This control was evident in their high press, with a PPDA of 6.1, which is significantly lower—meaning a much harder press—than the opponent’s 11.0. Brighton were successful in their strategy, maintaining their 3-2-5 shape in possession.

The match was defined by moments of chaos. A huge turning point came in the 19th minute when Brighton secured a high regain, leading to a goal for #9 Harvey Radley, which set the tone. Although Manchester United scored the opener in the 41st minute on the counter, Brighton responded fiercely. The decisive moment was the 63rd minute goal by #5 Isaac Kane-Moss from a set piece, confirming Brighton’s superiority.
